newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Most Brazilians think land should be given to poor.
newsitem.headline: Most Brazilians think land should be given to poor.

text.p: Most Brazilians, influenced by a popular soap opera, favour confiscating unproductive land from powerful landowners and handing it over to the poor, according to a survey published on Thursday.

The poll for Brazil's private National Industry Confederation (CNI) found that 88 percent of people questioned thought the government should adopt a radical confiscation programme to even the spread of land distribution.
CNI President Fernando Bezerra told reporters that television had made many more Brazilians aware of the need for agrarian reform than in the past.
"Society has become aware of the problem of land in Brazil and I think it has a lot to do with that soap opera, Rei do Gado," Bezerra said.

"Rei do Gado" (King of Cattle), a popular soap opera that ran until this's year's annual carnival on national Globo television, told the story of a wealthy landowner who fell in love with a beautiful landless girl.
The Roman Catholic Church, a champion of the dispossessed in Brazil, says 46 percent of arable land in Latin America's largest country is in the hands of just one percent of landowners.

The militant Landless Movement (MST), which claims to represent five million homeless families, has been occupying disused farms by force in an attempt to pressure the government into pressing on with land reform.

The militant tactics of the MST have led to frequent clashes between peasants and armed farmhands. Next month marks the first anniversary of the massacre of 19 squatters by military police in the northern state of Para.
The CNI survey showed that 94 percent of Brazilians supported the MST's cause but thought the fight for land reform should be conducted without violence.
